candidate.blueprint_locator: Psychosocial Integrity: assess coping and psychosocial needs, use therapeutic communication, support adjustment to chronic illness, and facilitate appropriate resources/referrals.
candidate.blueprint_topic: Psychosocial Integrity — long-term adjustment to HIV
candidate.educational_objective: Support long-term HIV adjustment through continuing, nonjudgmental assessment of emotional, social, adherence, and structural needs and connection to appropriate mental-health, navigation, case-management, peer, and community resources.

options.A: Use ongoing nonjudgmental conversations to identify emotional, social, adherence, and structural barriers and connect the client with mental-health, case-management, navigation, peer/support-group, and other services as needed.
options.B: Limit support to one conversation at diagnosis because psychosocial needs generally end once antiretroviral therapy begins.
options.C: Focus only on whether doses are taken and avoid discussing mental health, stigma, relationships, housing, transportation, or social support.
options.D: Assume that viral suppression eliminates the need for continuing psychosocial assessment or support.

candidate.rationale: A is correct. CDC's current HIV clinical-care guidance recommends regular conversations at every office visit to identify adherence barriers and links psychosocial barriers such as depression, substance use, negative beliefs about HIV, low quality of life, and lack of social support with the need for support services. CDC specifically identifies patient navigators, psychologists, support groups, adherence counselors, case managers, and referrals for structural barriers such as transportation, housing, childcare, and insurance. B, C, and D incorrectly treat HIV care as medication-only or time-limited support.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Long-term HIV care includes recurring assessment and support for psychosocial and structural barriers, not medication adherence alone; referrals and navigation/support services should be used as needs evolve.
candidate.source_document_title: Clinical Care of HIV — HIV Nexus
candidate.source_locator: 'Help your patients adhere to ART by engaging in regular conversations at every office visit': identify barriers and offer adherence/support services. 'Psychosocial barriers to adherence': mental health issues, substance use, negative HIV beliefs and lack of social support; refer to psychologists, support groups, adherence counselors, case managers and patient navigators. 'Structural barriers': transportation, housing, childcare and insurance; connect with navigation and support. 'Keeping patients in care': build supportive relationships and refer to needed mental-health/social services.
candidate.source_organization: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC)
candidate.stem: A client has recently been diagnosed with HIV and says, 'I don't know how I will manage this for the rest of my life.' Which nursing plan best supports long-term adjustment?
